text.p: Mozambique's central bank on Saturday announced an easing of restrictions on the amount of money travellers can take in and out of the country.

Currently customs officials can demand proof that foreign currency being taken out of Mozambique was obtained legally -- though in practice they do not usually trouble travellers carrying small amounts.
The new regulation, published in full by the Maputo daily Noticias on Saturday, said up to $5,000 can be brought into the country without being declared.

Banco de Mocambique governor Adriano Maleiane told a news conference this meant the same amount could be taken out again without declaration, even though it is not specifically stated in the regulation.
The amount of meticais that can be taken out of the country rises from 500 (about $00.04) to 500,000 ($43).
Maleiane said the bank would meet police and customs officials to explain the changes, which come into force when they are published in the government gazette. This could take up to a month.
